title: Nephi’s words to his brethren
summary: Nephi tells his brethren that he has spoken as constrained by the Spirit, expresses certainty that what he spoke will come to pass, and says that things written out of the book will be of great worth.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he has spoken to his brethren as constrained by the Spirit and knows that what he spoke must come to pass.
Nephi says that things written out of the book will be of great worth to the children of men, especially their seed, a remnant of the house of Israel.

unspecified_visual_details: The brethren’s individual identities and appearances.
The setting and whether the book is physically present.

spoken_dialogue.text: I have spoken unto you, according as the Spirit hath constrained me;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: wherefore, I know that they must surely come to pass.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: And the things which shall be written out of the book shall be of great worth unto the children of men, and especially unto our seed, which is a remnant of the house of Israel.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The predicted fulfillment and worth of the writings are Nephi’s statements, not events shown occurring here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Spirit with an invented visible appearance.
Do not depict predicted events as occurring in this scene.
Do not invent identities for the brethren or assume the book is physically present.

title: Churches contend
summary: Nephi describes churches not built unto the Lord claiming the Lord's authority and contending, as do their priests.

explicit_facts.text: Churches not built unto the Lord will claim to belong to the Lord, and contend with one another.
Their priests will contend, teach with their learning, and deny the Holy Ghost, which gives utterance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This is a prophecy reported by Nephi, not a present-time event; it can be conveyed through narration over a neutral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The churches, their members, priests, place, and period are not specified.

narration.text: the churches which are built up, and not unto the Lord
they shall contend one with another

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The claims and conflict are future events described in prophecy; do not stage them as a witnessed present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign denominations, names, or identifying appearances to the churches or priests.

title: Denial of God's power
summary: Nephi warns that people will deny God's power and teach that God no longer works miracles.

explicit_facts.text: People will deny the power of God and tell others there is no God today, saying the Lord and Redeemer has finished his work and given his power to men.
They will teach people not to believe reports of miracles, saying God is no longer a God of miracles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be presented as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The speakers, listeners, location, and any claimed miracles are not identified.

narration.text: they deny the power of God, the Holy One of Israel
he is not a God of miracles

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is prophetic reporting and a false teaching; no miracle or divine appearance is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a miracle, God, or the Redeemer appearing.

title: Many Shall Say
summary: Nephi forecasts sayings that encourage eating, drinking, and merriment in anticipation of death. He also forecasts claims excusing wrongdoing and promising light punishment followed by salvation.

explicit_facts.text: Many are forecast to say that they should eat, drink, and be merry because tomorrow they die and it shall be well with them.
Many are also forecast to claim that God will justify committing a little sin, including lying, taking advantage of another because of his words, and digging a pit for a neighbor.
These predicted speakers claim that, if guilty, they will receive a few stripes from God and ultimately be saved in God's kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A text-based presentation can preserve the sayings as forecasts without staging their fulfillment.
unspecified_visual_details: No physical setting, appearance, clothing, gestures, or audience is specified.
The predicted speakers and their neighbors are not individually identified.

narration.text: Yea, and there shall be many which shall say: Eat, drink, and be merry, for tomorrow we die; and it shall be well with us.
And there shall also be many which shall say: Eat, drink, and be merry; nevertheless, fear God—he will justify in committing a little sin;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is the narrator, as established by the supplied chapter context; narration excerpts retain his forecasting language.
The predicted sayings are reported claims, not Nephi's counsel or established promises from God.
No fulfillment of these predictions is narrated in these verses.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the predicted speakers as a present gathering or assign their sayings to present-tense dialogue.
Do not depict eating, drinking, lying, exploitation, pit digging, punishment, death, or salvation as occurring events.
Do not invent an appearance of God.
Do not invent names, biographies, listeners, or a physical setting for Nephi.

title: Works in the dark
summary: Many shall teach false, vain, and foolish doctrines, hide their counsels from the Lord, and have works in the dark. The blood of the saints shall cry from the ground against them.

explicit_facts.text: Many shall teach false, vain, and foolish doctrines, be puffed up in their hearts, seek to hide their counsels from the Lord, and have works in the dark.
The blood of the saints shall cry from the ground against them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Darkness can suggest concealed works without depicting a particular act.
unspecified_visual_details: The teachers, saints, setting, and nature of the works are unspecified.

narration.text: and their works shall be in the dark.
And the blood of the saints shall cry from the ground against them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blood crying from the ground is figurative language, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood, wounds, or a literal speaking manifestation of blood.

title: Pride corrupts churches
summary: Nephi says people have gone astray and become corrupted, and attributes the corruption of their churches to pride, false teachers, and false doctrine.

explicit_facts.text: The people have gone out of the way and become corrupted.
Pride, false teachers, and false doctrine have corrupted their churches, which are lifted up; the people are puffed up with pride.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The description is prophetic and may be conveyed through narration without staging a specific event.
unspecified_visual_details: The churches, people, architecture, and time are unspecified.

narration.text: they have all gone out of the way; they have become corrupted.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: No particular church or group is named.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the churches or people invented identities.

title: The poor and meek are mistreated
summary: Nephi describes the proud taking from the poor, persecuting the meek, and erring under the precepts of men; a few remain humble followers of Christ.

explicit_facts.text: The people rob the poor because of their fine sanctuaries and clothing and persecute the meek and poor in heart.
Most have gone astray; a few are humble followers of Christ, yet in many instances they err because they are taught by men's precepts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The mistreatment can be represented without specifying a particular victim or physical assault.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, clothing, sanctuaries, and specific acts of taking or persecution are not detailed.

narration.text: They rob the poor because of their fine sanctuaries
they persecute the meek and the poor in heart

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chapter gives a general prophetic description, not an account of a particular incident.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named perpetrators or victims or depict explicit violence.

title: A warning to the proud
summary: Nephi pronounces woe upon the proud, false teachers, and those who pervert the Lord's way, and warns those who reject what is good.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God Almighty pronounces woe on the proud wise, learned, and rich, false teachers, those who commit whoredoms, and those who pervert the Lord's way; they will be thrust down to hell.
Those who turn aside the just and revile what is good will face a future day of visitation; the fully iniquitous will perish.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning may be carried by narration over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The individuals, their actions, and any future visitation are not described as occurring now.

narration.text: wo, wo, wo be unto them
revile against that which is good

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prophetic warning, not a depiction of people being cast into hell.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine figure, judgment, or hell as a present visual event.

title: Repentance and the fall of the great church
summary: Nephi says the inhabitants of the earth will not be destroyed if they repent, and prophesies that the great and abominable church will fall.

explicit_facts.text: The inhabitants of the earth who repent of wickedness and abominations will not be destroyed, the Lord of Hosts says.
The great and abominable church will tumble to the earth and have a great fall.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The church's fall may be suggested symbolically; its identity and physical appearance are not specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The church's form, setting, and timing are unspecified.

narration.text: if the inhabitants of the earth shall repent
that great and abominable church

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The church's fall is a future prophecy, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a recognizable church, its members, or a literal collapse scene.

title: Anger against what is good
summary: Nephi warns that the devil's kingdom will shake and that the devil will stir people to anger against what is good.

explicit_facts.text: The devil's kingdom must shake; its people must be stirred to repentance or the devil will grasp them with everlasting chains, stir them to anger, and they will perish.
The devil will rage in the hearts of people and stir them to anger against what is good.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The language about shaking, grasping, and rage in hearts is figurative and can be conveyed through narration rather than literal supernatural imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, setting, and any literal visual form for the devil or chains are unspecified.

narration.text: stir them up to anger against that which is good.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses teach through figures of speech; no visible devil or supernatural chains are narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil, chains, or a kingdom physically shaking.

title: Lulled into security
summary: Nephi says the devil will lull some into carnal security so they say all is well in Zion. He will flatter others, tell them there is no hell, and deny that he is a devil.

explicit_facts.text: The devil will pacify some into carnal security, and they will say all is well in Zion.
The devil will cheat their souls and lead them away.
The devil will flatter others, tell them there is no hell, deny that he is a devil, and grasp them with chains from which there is no deliverance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi's warning can be presented without depicting the foretold events as happening now.
unspecified_visual_details: No setting or physical appearances are specified.
The people in the two groups are unnamed.

spoken_dialogue.text: All is well in Zion; yea, Zion prospereth, all is well
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Others

spoken_dialogue.text: I am no devil, for there is none
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The devil

narration.text: And others will he pacify, and lull them away into carnal security, that they will say:
And behold, others he flattereth away, and telleth them there is no hell; and he saith unto them:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The claims that all is well, that there is no hell, and that there is no devil are attributed to the deceived people or the devil, not endorsed by Nephi.
The verses describe future deception; they do not narrate a present encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil's appearance or literal chains.
Do not invent identities, a setting, or additional dialogue for either group.

title: Judgment and the place prepared
summary: Nephi says those seized by death, hell, and the devil must stand before God's throne, be judged according to their works, and go to the place prepared for them.

explicit_facts.text: Those seized by death, hell, and the devil must stand before God's throne, be judged according to their works, and go to the place prepared for them, described as a lake of fire and brimstone and endless torment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This is a future judgment described in prophecy, not a present-time scene.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance of God, throne, judged individuals, or the place is described.

narration.text: must stand before the throne of God
be judged according to their works

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports a future judgment; it does not describe the throne or depict the event occurring now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent God's appearance or stage the future judgment as a present event.

title: Warnings to those at ease
summary: Nephi warns those at ease in Zion, those who cry that all is well, those who heed men's precepts and deny God's power and the gift of the Holy Ghost, and those who say they need no more.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi pronounces woe on one who is at ease in Zion.
Nephi pronounces woe on one who cries that all is well.
Nephi pronounces woe on one who heeds the precepts of men and denies the power of God and the gift of the Holy Ghost.
Nephi pronounces woe on one who says they have received and need no more.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi's warnings can be presented as narration without depicting the people he describes.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance and physical surroundings are unspecified.
No particular gathering or visible location in Zion is described.

narration.text: Therefore, wo be unto him that is at ease in Zion!
Wo be unto him that crieth: All is well!
Yea, wo be unto him that hearkeneth unto the precepts of men, and denieth the power of God, and the gift of the Holy Ghost!
Yea, wo be unto him that saith: We have received, and we need no more!

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses are warnings, not accounts of visible events. The quoted claims are framed as things people say, not as dialogue occurring in a depicted gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Zion as the scene's established location or invent identifiable inhabitants.
Do not depict God or the Holy Ghost; no appearance is described.
Do not stage the reported claims as a new conversation.

title: Rock and sandy foundation
summary: Nephi warns those who tremble and are angry because of God's truth, contrasts receiving it gladly with fearing a fall, and warns against saying that no more of God's word is needed.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi pronounces woe upon those who tremble and are angry because of the truth of God.
The person built upon the rock receives it with gladness; the person built upon a sandy foundation trembles lest he fall.
Nephi pronounces woe upon one who says they have received God's word and need no more of it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The rock and sandy foundation are figures in Nephi's teaching, not a narrated construction event.
unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance and surroundings are not specified.
The person who says they need no more of God's word is not identified or visually described.

narration.text: For behold, he that is built upon the rock receiveth it with gladness; and he that is built upon a sandy foundation trembleth lest he shall fall.
Wo be unto him that shall say: We have received the word of God, and we need no more of the word of God, for we have enough!

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 29 presents a hypothetical person's words within Nephi's warning; it does not narrate someone speaking in a particular scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal building or a person standing on rock or sand as a narrated event.
Do not invent an identity or appearance for the person described in verse 29.

title: Line upon line
summary: Nephi quotes the Lord's teaching that people receive line upon line, and that those who listen to his counsel learn wisdom and receive more; he curses those who trust in man and men's precepts.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God says he will give the children of men knowledge line upon line, and blesses those who heed his precepts and counsel; those who receive will be given more, while those who say they have enough will lose what they have.
The Lord curses those who trust in man or heed men's precepts unless those precepts are given by the power of the Holy Ghost.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This teaching may be rendered as off-screen narration without showing the Lord.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible divine appearance, audience, or setting is specified.

narration.text: line upon line, precept upon precept
blessed are those who hearken unto my precepts

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chapter quotes the Lord's words but does not describe a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord appearing or invent a scene in which he speaks visibly.

title: The Lord's extended mercy
summary: Nephi relays the Lord's warning that the Gentiles will deny him despite his continual offer of mercy. The Lord says he will be merciful if they repent and come unto him.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord pronounces woe to the Gentiles and says they will deny him despite his extended arm.
The Lord says he will be merciful to them if they repent and come unto him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi's account can be conveyed through narration without depicting the Lord or the Gentiles.
The extended arm is figurative in this teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearances of Nephi and the Gentiles are unspecified.

narration.text: Wo be unto the Gentiles, saith the Lord God of Hosts!
I will be merciful unto them, saith the Lord God, if they will repent and come unto me;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The narration retains the verse's attribution to the Lord; its first-person promise is not Nephi's own speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine arm or visible divine figure.
Do not stage a new encounter with the Gentiles.
